### Modifications in Files

**File: `ClusterResourceProvider.java`**
- Introduced a new `HashSet<String>` named `encounteredConfigTypes` to track configuration types that have been added during the process.
- Modified the logic within the existing loop that processes service configuration types:
  - Implemented a check to ensure that each configuration type is added to the `blueprintConfigRequest` only if it has not been previously encountered, effectively preventing duplicate additions of the same configuration type.
  - Kept the existing logic to skip handling of the "cluster-env" config type as before.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The new `encounteredConfigTypes` set serves as a mechanism to enforce uniqueness for the configuration types added to the `blueprintConfigRequest`. The modification addresses a specific bug (AMBARI-8867) by ensuring that each configuration type is handled no more than once during the deployment process. This change is described as a temporary fix to unblock another related bug (BUG-28939) while indicating that a more comprehensive solution will be provided as part of a future fix (BUG-29145). Thus, these modifications are interconnected, as the introduction of the `HashSet` directly impacts how configuration types are processed, relating to several bugs within the system.

This can lead to conflicts or errors if the same configuration type is set with different values during the blueprint deployment process.

```java
Collection<String> encounteredConfigTypes = new HashSet<String>();
if (encounteredConfigTypes.add(serviceConfigType)) {
```

The addition of a `HashSet` called `encounteredConfigTypes` ensures that each configuration type is only added once. The `add` method of the `HashSet` returns `false` if the item already exists, thus preventing duplicate configuration types from being processed and added to the `blueprintConfigRequest`, thereby resolving the issue of potential conflicts in cluster configuration.
